messages:
Acme Ops: Hey team — we've got recurring disconnects from our webapp to the Redwood streaming endpoint. Happens ~10-15m into a session, client sees partial output and then a reconnect loop. No obvious errors client-side except socket closed.

Liz (Support): Sorry you're seeing this — can you share a minimal repro and timestamps? are you using our hosted API or Dedicated?

Acme Ops: Hosted. Repro steps: open SSE at /v1/stream with Authorization header, send a long generation (expected ~60s), after 10-15m the stream drops during idle periods. We tried reconnecting with Last-Event-ID and sometimes resume, sometimes not. First drop was 2028-03-06T15:34:20Z, then 15:49:35Z.

Aj (Eng Runtime): Quiet question: is the client idle while waiting for server events? Or are tokens coming through continuously?

Acme Ops: Mostly idle. We send occasional user typing events but no token traffic for a while. When there's silence the connection seems more likely to die.

Sam (SRE): This smells like an intermediate proxy / load balancer idle timeout. What does the infra path look like? Are you going through an ALB / Cloudflare / nginx?

Acme Ops: Behind our CDN (Cloudflare) -> ALB on AWS -> ECS service. We've seen ALB idle timeout is default 60s, but this is happening far after that.

Marta (DevEx): Can you paste the exact client SSE open call and a short server-side keepalive implementation? Even a curl reproduce is helpful.

Acme Ops: Sure — client code (simplified):

```
const es = new EventSource('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream', { headers: { Authorization: 'Bearer xyz' } });
es.onmessage = (e) => console.log('tok', e.data);
es.onerror = () => console.log('sse error');
```

Server-side we rely on the platform stream, no custom pings.

Liz (Support): Thanks. Two quick angles: 1) platform will send occasional comment pings to keep idle proxies from closing, but behavior depends on path. 2) TCP keepalive is separate and might be disabled on some hops.

Aj (Eng Runtime): Can you share TCP-level logs from client side? Also, do you see any 502/504 in the ALB or Cloudflare logs? If ALB closes due to target health or idle timeout then it will send FIN to client.

Acme Ops: ALB logs show many requests with target:active and some entries with ELB status code 504 around the drop times. Cloudflare shows 524 occasionally. No 502.

Sam (SRE): 504/524 indicates origin took too long to respond to a Cloudflare/ALB healthcheck or the connection was terminated midstream. For long-lived SSE, we usually recommend explicit comment pings every 15-30s (e.g., `:\n`) to keep proxies alive. Does Redwood send comment pings for hosted streams?

Aj (Eng Runtime): Hosted streams do send comment pings, but there are caveats: if an intermediate proxy buffers or coalesces traffic and then enforces a higher-level idle window, pings might not traverse or be considered insufficient. Also HTTP/2 vs HTTP/1.1 path differences — ALB to backend on HTTP/1.1 can time out differently.

Marta (DevEx): Quick repro plan: 1) Have Acme run a small client that opens SSE and sends periodic `ping` events from server every 15s (comment line `:\n` or `: keepalive\n`). 2) Toggle Cloudflare 'disable http2' to force http1.1 and see difference. 3) Set ALB idle timeout to 350s while testing.

Acme Ops: Will try. Also curious about config on Redwood side — any headers we should look for (Connection, Keep-Alive)?

Liz (Support): We'll check server logs for your sessions. Can you share a sample session ID or request ID next time it happens? Our logs include `x-rw-req-id` on responses.

deploy-bot: deployment redeployed service/api 2028-03-06T15:40:02Z by Aj (Eng Runtime) :rocket:

Aj (Eng Runtime): Noted. If you can reproduce, please run `tcpdump` on client or show `ss -tnp` to see if the socket is in FIN_WAIT or RST. Example commands: `sudo tcpdump -i eth0 port 443` and `ss -o state established '( sport = :443 )'`. Also capture ALB access logs and target group health events around drop time.

Acme Ops: Quick test done — added server comment pings every 15s and set ALB idle timeout to 350s. After 2 hours still connected. Looks promising. Will run longer tests and report.

Sam (SRE): Nice. One more gotcha: if client OS drops idle TCP connections (mobile networks, NAT timeouts) you might need client-side TCP keepalive or application-level reconnection with resume tokens. For SSE resume semantics we recommend storing partial KV cache and replaying from last-event-id.

Marta (DevEx): I'll draft a short how-to we can share: include curl repro, recommended server comment ping code (node/python snippet), ALB/nginx tunables, and client reconnection pattern with Last-Event-ID.

Aj (Eng Runtime): For reference, Node SSE keepalive snippet we use internally:

```
res.writeHead(200, { 'Content-Type': 'text/event-stream', 'Cache-Control': 'no-cache', Connection: 'keep-alive' });
const keep = setInterval(() => { try { res.write(':\n'); } catch (e) { clearInterval(keep); } }, 15000);
// on finish: clearInterval(keep);
```

Liz (Support): Thanks everyone. @Acme Ops please ping this thread with the next drop (if any) and the `x-rw-req-id` value. If pinging fixes it we'll add a KB entry on comment pings + ALB/cloudflare guidance. :thumbsup:

Acme Ops: Will do. Thanks all — hope this helps others.
